input.context: James Hutton is often viewed as the first modern geologist. In 1785 he presented a paper entitled Theory of the Earth to the Royal Society of Edinburgh. In his paper, he explained his theory that the Earth must be much older than had previously been supposed in order to allow enough time for mountains to be eroded and for sediments to form new rocks at the bottom of the sea, which in turn were raised up to become dry land. Hutton published a two-volume version of his ideas in 1795 (Vol. 1, Vol. 2).

Context:
James Hutton is often viewed as the first modern geologist. In 1785 he presented a paper entitled Theory of the Earth to the Royal Society of Edinburgh. In his paper, he explained his theory that the Earth must be much older than had previously been supposed in order to allow enough time for mountains to be eroded and for sediments to form new rocks at the bottom of the sea, which in turn were raised up to become dry land. Hutton published a two-volume version of his ideas in 1795 (Vol. 1, Vol. 2).

Question:
Why did the Royal Society think the Earth was older than previously thought?

response.prediction: The Royal Society did not think the Earth was older; rather, James Hutton proposed in his 1785 paper to the Royal Society of Edinburgh that the Earth must be much older than previously supposed. He argued that a longer timescale was necessary to account for geological processes such as the erosion of mountains and the formation of new rocks from sediments at the bottom of the sea, which later become land. The context does not say the Royal Society already thought the Earth was older; instead, Hutton was presenting a new and controversial idea that challenged the shorter timescales previously accepted.
